important.name: A merged pull request in an override never hides
important.summary: `ghStateOf` keeps only `OPEN` and `CLOSED` and maps every other state to `UNKNOWN`, which `isClosed` always shows. `gh ... --json state` reports `MERGED` for a merged pull request, so a PR number in an override stays on every branch's line indefinitely and is rechecked every `todo.gh.max_age_hours`. If `gh issue view` refuses a PR number instead, the failure path also lands on `UNKNOWN`, with the same result. This defeats the PR-number case the change explicitly plans for: hide.test.ts:95-99 says a PR number in an override 'shows until gh answers CLOSED', and the README says the same. A merged PR, the normal way a PR ends, never gets that answer. The pure test passes because it injects `CLOSED` directly, so nothing exercises the gh mapping.
fix: In `ghStateOf`, map `MERGED` to `CLOSED` (`state === 'MERGED' ? 'CLOSED' : ...`), and add a watch.test.ts case where gh answers `MERGED` and the number hides.
If `gh issue view` turns out to reject PR numbers, retry the same number with `gh pr view <n> --json state` before recording `UNKNOWN`, and treat `MERGED` as closed there too.

important.name: A failed issue-cache write turns recheck and scan into an endless gh loop
important.summary:
runRecheck swallows a failed cache write (`$.fs.write(...).catch(noop)`, watch.ts:448) and still calls requestScan when a gh answer changed an issue's hiding (watch.ts:450). The scan reads the old cache from disk, so the issue is still due, and runScan always queues another recheck (watch.ts:430). That recheck runs gh for the same issues again, sees the same change against the same stale disk cache, and requests another scan. While the cache file cannot be written (read-only or locked state dir, full disk), the session runs `gh issue view` for every due issue in a loop with no end, up to 10 s per call and invisible to the user.

Also (adv_code_runtime): runRecheck swallows a failed write of issues.json (`.catch(noop)`) but still compares the closed state against its in-memory `next` map and calls requestScan when an issue's hiding changed. The scan rereads the unchanged cache from disk, finds the same issue still due (its on-disk answer is old or absent), and ends with `later(... requestRecheck)`; the recheck runs gh again, sees the same in-memory-vs-disk difference, and asks for another scan. Nothing breaks the cycle while the write keeps failing, so the mod spawns `gh issue view` (and a full scan with git calls) back to back for as long as the session lives, which contradicts the module's promise that a host failure degrades to an empty line.

Also (overall): When dueIssues comes back empty, runRecheck returns at line 445 without updating memo.recheckDueAt. That happens when another session in the same checkout has already rewritten issues.json, or when the answers moved later in some other way that the last scan did not see. isRecheckDue (lines 504-507) then stays true, and every prompt schedules a recheck pass (resolveWatch plus four file reads) that finds nothing due and returns, until an unrelated scan recomputes the memo. No gh call is wasted, but the pass repeats on every prompt.

Attack: Project with an override naming issue 301 (`working 301` on any branch), no `<state_dir>/working-refs/issues.json` and no open list, and issue 301 closed on GitHub. Make the cache unwritable (create `<state_dir>/working-refs/issues.json` with `{}` and mark it read-only, or stub `$.fs.write` to reject for that path in a hook test). Start a session: runScan (watch.ts:402) ends with `later(requestRecheck)` (430); runRecheck finds 301 due (answeredAt -Infinity), gh answers CLOSED, the write at 448 fails silently, `isClosed(301, list, hide.cache)` is false while `isClosed(301, list, next)` is true, so 450 calls requestScan; the scan rereads the unchanged file, line 430 queues another recheck, 301 is due again, and the cycle repeats. Counting `$.process.run` calls with argv[0] === 'gh' over a few clock ticks shows it growing without bound instead of stopping at 1.
fix: Treat the write as a precondition for the follow-up scan: `const wrote = await $.fs.write(path, text).then(() => true, () => false)`, and return before requestScan when it is false, after setting memo.recheckDueAt to now + maxAgeOf(w) so a prompt does not retry at once.

Keep the session's attempts in memory (for example `memo.attempts: Map<number, CachedIssue>` merged over the disk cache in readHide), so a failed write does not drop the `triedAt` that stops dueIssues from picking the issue again.
In runRecheck, request the follow-up scan only when the cache write succeeded (await the write without `.catch(noop)` inside a try, and return on failure).
Keep the rechecked cache in session memory (for example `memo.cache`) and have the scan merge it over the file, so a failed write cannot make the same issue due again.
Gate the scan-end `later(... requestRecheck)` on `memo.recheckDueAt <= now`, so a scan triggered by a recheck does not start another recheck before the due time passes.
Before the early return in runRecheck, set memo.recheckDueAt = dueAtOf(issues, hide.list, hide.cache, maxAgeOf(w)), so the probe waits for the real next due time.

minor.name: Plan 2027 names branch 1171-banner-todo-fixup; the work lands from 2171-banner-todo-fixup
minor.summary:
The frozen ActionPlan sets "branch": "1171-banner-todo-fixup" (line 6) and the PIP head repeats it ("Branch 1171-banner-todo-fixup -> main", PIP line 107), while the PR branch is 2171-banner-todo-fixup (both branches exist locally). working-refs rule 1 compares the plan's `branch` with the current branch, and rule 2 does not hold either (base_commit 1043312 is not the PR's merge base 22e33d8), so the feature's own plan link and its refs (todo-k69m, #301) never show on the branch that ships it, and the PIP misnames the branch it records.

Also (overall): The ActionPlan's `branch` is `1171-banner-todo-fixup` (line 6), and the PIP head row says the same (PIP line 107), but the PR head branch is `2171-banner-todo-fixup`. A local branch named 1171 also exists, so the work appears to have moved to the 2171 branch. working-refs rule 1 (plan branch equals the current branch) therefore never holds on the PR branch. Rule 2 does not hold either: base_commit 1043312 differs from the branch's merge base with main, 22e33d8. So the plan 2027 link never appears on this branch's working line, though its own feature exists to show it.

Also (roast): The ActionPlan's `branch` is `1171-banner-todo-fixup` and its `base_commit` is `1043312`, but this PR's branch is `2171-banner-todo-fixup` with merge base `22e33d8`. So rule 1 (branch name) and rule 2 (merge base) of `qualifies` both fail here, and the working line on this branch never shows plan 2027, the plan for the working line itself. The PIP page head row repeats the old branch.
fix: Refreeze plan 2027 through the plan driver with `branch` set to 2171-banner-todo-fixup (plan_api.write, then plan.py freeze, which re-renders the PIP), with the developer's OK.
If the rename to 2171 is the accident, rename the branch back so the plan, the PIP and the receipts name the branch the work came from.
Refreeze plan 2027 with `branch` set to `2171-banner-todo-fixup` through the plan driver (a routine refreeze), which re-renders the PIP head row.
Leave it, since the plan stops qualifying after the merge anyway, and note the branch move in the PR description.
Set `branch` to `2171-banner-todo-fixup` (and `base_commit` to the current merge base if rule 2 should hold), then refreeze and re-render the PIP page per the plan workflow.
Leave it as is if the plan is archived at merge, and note in the PR description that the plan link does not show on this branch.

minor.name: band-line copies the line's join rules with nothing tying them to working-refs
minor.summary: `workingParts` rebuilds the line from `head`, `others` and `more` using its own copy of working-refs's `compose` rules: ` · ` only when both sides exist, a space between segments, and ` +N` with a space only when something precedes it. The spec picked approach A so that format lives 'in one place', but this is a second place. Every band.test.tsx fixture hand-writes a `text` that matches the parts, so if `compose` in line.ts changes, band-line silently draws a different string from the `text` the same atom carries and no test notices.
fix: In `workingParts`, join the plain parts (each `{dim}` as its string) and return `[line.text]` when the result differs from `line.text`, so the drawn characters always equal the producer's text. Add a band.test.tsx case with a mismatched `text` that draws `text` verbatim.

minor.name: setup-statusline summary text omits the new replace-old-widget path
minor.summary:
Step 5 now offers to replace an existing widget's `commandPath` when it names `working-refs/line.txt` (SKILL.md:73-75), but the frontmatter description (line 3: "the defaults when absent, else only the opt-in working-refs line"), the Files written table (line 21: "an existing file only gains the working-refs line, on a yes in step 5"), the step 7 report (lines 97-98: only "whether the working-refs line was added") and the banner-status README bullet (README.md:43-45: "on a yes appends only the working-refs custom-command line") still say an existing file can only gain the line. Step 5 also does not name the question tool or header for the replace offer, unlike the add offer beside it.

Also (skill_package): Step 5 (SKILL.md:73-75) now also rewrites an existing widget's commandPath when it names working-refs/line.txt. The skill's Files-written table (SKILL.md:21: 'an existing file only gains the working-refs line, on a yes in step 5'), its frontmatter description (SKILL.md:3: 'else only the opt-in working-refs line') and the banner-status README (README.md:23 'only gains the working-refs line on a yes', README.md:43-45) still say that adding the line is the only change made to an existing file. The skill's own summary therefore contradicts its step 5.

Also (skill_package): Step 5 (SKILL.md:74-75) says to 'offer to replace that widget's commandPath' but, unlike the add-the-line offer right after it, does not say to use AskUserQuestion, which header to use or what the options are. Step 7 (SKILL.md:97-98) reports only 'whether the working-refs line was added', so a commandPath that was replaced or kept never appears in the report.
fix: SKILL.md line 3 and line 21: add that an existing widget naming working-refs/line.txt can have its commandPath replaced on a yes; step 7: report whether the old widget was replaced; step 5: ask the replace offer with AskUserQuestion (header working-refs); banner-status README.md:43-45: add the same sentence.

Change SKILL.md:21 to say an existing file gains the working-refs line, or has an old line.txt widget's commandPath replaced, on a yes in step 5. Make the same change to the description at SKILL.md:3 and to plugins/banner-status/README.md:23 and :43-45.

At SKILL.md:74-75, ask with AskUserQuestion (header `working-refs`) and two options, **Replace the command** and **Keep the file as it is**. At SKILL.md:97-98, report whether the working-refs line was added, replaced or kept.

minor.name: working-refs README still says the line is empty with no override, though other branches' overrides now fill it
minor.summary: README.md:19 says "Nothing qualifies and no override: the line is empty" and the State table (line 95) says `line` is null "while nothing qualifies or overrides". With this change buildLine (line.ts:103-108) draws every other branch's visible override even when the current branch has no plan and no override of its own, so the line is empty only when nothing qualifies and no branch has a visible override (or before git-status's first snapshot, watch.ts:418).

minor.name: "Every branch means one checkout" ignores the absolute state_dir case the same README documents
minor.summary: plugins/working-refs/README.md:40-41 states that overrides.json and both issue files live under the checkout's own state_dir, "so a d-w worktree session does not see the main checkout's overrides". Lines 107-108 of the same file (and config.ts `under`, which keeps an absolute path) say an absolute state_dir is shared by every checkout, in which case a worktree session does see the main checkout's overrides. The two paragraphs contradict each other for that configuration.
fix: plugins/working-refs/README.md:40-41: qualify the sentence with "(with a relative state_dir; an absolute one is shared, and every checkout then sees the same overrides)".

minor.name: README says every scan rewrites each line file; line.json is skipped before the first snapshot
minor.summary: plugins/working-refs/README.md:107-111 states that after every scan the rendered text is compared with each line file's contents and rewritten on any difference, so the session.start scan empties a line another branch or an earlier session left. watch.ts:429 writes line.json only when `branch !== null`, so a session.start scan that runs before git-status's first snapshot leaves an earlier session's line.json as it was (the plan's TASK-5 asks for exactly that). The same README's Files table (line 103) already says line.json is 'Not written before git-status's first snapshot', so the paragraph contradicts the row above it.
fix: Qualify the paragraph: line.txt is compared and rewritten after every scan; line.json only after scans that have a git-status snapshot, so a line.json from an earlier session stays (its branch stamp tells the widget it is stale) until the first snapshot.

Separately, optionalPathOr (lines 50-52) has the same body as pathOr (lines 47-48) and differs only in the fallback's type.
fix: Reword line 21 to 'The harness values the mod reads: paths (project-relative or absolute POSIX), the gh settings and the line cap', and line 23 to 'the override, line and issue-cache files live under <state_dir>/working-refs/, the open-issue list under <state_dir>/todo-sync/'. Make pathOr generic, `const pathOr = <T extends string | null>(v: unknown, fallback: T): string | T => ...`, and delete optionalPathOr.

minor.name: line.json's 'absent stays absent while there is no line' branch is untested
minor.summary: watch.ts:364-373 (writeLineJson) skips the write when no file exists and the text is empty, so a branch with nothing to show never creates line.json. The new 'line.json (plan 2027)' block in watch.test.ts tests the stamped write, the no-snapshot skip and the rewrite of an existing file, but no test covers a snapshot with no line and no existing file. If that guard were removed, line.json would be written on every scan of an empty branch and no test would fail. Also, the test named 'a line that empties rewrites an existing line.json' never has a line in the session. It only covers a stale file from another branch.
fix: Add a test: world(on) with no plans or overrides, start, then expect(fileJson(w, LINE_JSON_FILE)).toBeUndefined() and expect(w.writes.map(keyOf)).not.toContain(keyOf(LINE_JSON_FILE)).
Rename the existing test to 'no line rewrites a stale line.json with empty text, stamped with the current branch'.

minor.name: Probe docstrings still describe the pre-2027 triggers
minor.summary:
afterToolCall's docstring (watch.ts:509) says a scan runs 'when the plans folder or the override file moved', but filesMoved (watch.ts:493-501) now also compares the catalog's and the open list's mtimes. WATCH_TOOLS (watch.ts:38) still says the watched tools 'may write a plan, its page or the override file' and leaves out the catalog and open_issues.json, which are the reason Bash/Edit calls now matter for hiding. onPrompt's docstring (watch.ts:516-520) lists branch, HEAD/tags and files, but the function now also queues a gh recheck when one is due (watch.ts:523).

Also (overall): Three prose contracts in watch.ts no longer match the code. The afterToolCall docstring (line 509) says a scan runs 'when the plans folder or the override file moved', but filesMoved (lines 493-501) now also compares the catalog and open_issues.json mtimes. The WATCH_TOOLS doc (line 38) lists only 'a plan, its page or the override file' as files those tools may write, though the catalog and the open list are now watched too. The module docstring (lines 25-26) says a scan runs 'when a recheck changed an issue's state', but runRecheck (line 450) asks for a scan only when an issue's hiding changes. An OPEN to UNKNOWN move, for example, triggers no scan. The runRecheck docstring and the README already state the narrower rule correctly.

Also (roast): `WATCH_TOOLS` (line 38) says its tools 'may write a plan, its page or the override file', and `afterToolCall` (line 509) says it scans 'when the plans folder or the override file moved'. `filesMoved` now also compares the catalog's and the open-issue list's mtimes, and the module header and README describe that, but these two comments were not updated.
fix: watch.ts:509: 'After a file or shell tool call: a scan when the plans folder, the override file, the catalog or the open-issue list moved.'
watch.ts:38: 'Tools whose calls may write a plan, its page, the override file, the TODO catalog or the open-issue list.'
watch.ts:516-520: add 'and a gh recheck pass when an override issue fell due (isRecheckDue)' to the onPrompt docstring.

watch.ts:509: 'a scan when the plans folder's signature or the mtime of the override file, the catalog or the open-issue list moved'; watch.ts:38: 'Tools whose calls may write a plan, its page, the override file, the catalog or the open-issue list'; watch.ts:25-26: 'and when a recheck changed whether an issue hides'.

Reword line 38 to name the catalog and the open-issue list as well, and line 509 to say 'when the plans folder's signature or the override file's, the catalog's or the open list's mtime moved' (the `filesMoved` wording).

minor.name: Open-issue list version is copied but never pinned across the mod/harness boundary
minor.summary: hide.ts:22-23 declares OPEN_LIST_VERSION = 1 as the version `todo_sync.issues.write_open_issues` writes, and openListOf drops any other version (fail-open: every issue shows). The harness side writes a literal 1 (issues.py:49). test_working_refs_contract.py's docstring (lines 6-10) says the open list is part of what the test keeps in step, and the new test at lines 86-92 pins only the path (OPEN_ISSUES_PATH), not the version. Each side pins its own literal 1 (hide.test.ts:30-38, test_todo_sync_open_issues.py:44), so bumping the Python version would update only the Python test, and the mod would then quietly ignore every list.
fix: Add a test to tests/mods/test_working_refs_contract.py that reads OPEN_LIST_VERSION (move it to mirror.ts, or read it from hide.ts with ts_number), calls issues.write_open_issues on a make_project config, and asserts the written `version` equals it.
Promote the literal in issues.py to a module constant (e.g. OPEN_ISSUES_VERSION) and pin the mirror against that constant.

minor.name: Module docstring still says the statusline contract is prose or data only
minor.summary: The docstring at test_setup_statusline_contract.py:7-8 ends with 'All of it is prose or data, so the test pins the shared names.' The new tests at lines 136-239 run the widget's node command in a subprocess and check what it prints (branch stamp, HEAD and worktree `.git` file resolution, the line.txt fallback). That is behavioral code under test, not a pin on shared names, so the docstring no longer describes the module.
fix: Reword the closing sentence, e.g.: 'The skill and defaults are prose or data, so most tests pin the shared names; the widget command is code, so its tests run it under node against a temporary checkout.'

minor.name: Widget path pin no longer tied to the harness LINE_JSON_REL constant
minor.summary:
The widget test previously imported harness_lib.working_refs.LINE_REL, so a rename on the producer side failed the widget test. It now spells `_LINE_JSON = "working-refs/line.json"` as a literal. The comment says this keeps the test independent of whether the harness constant has landed, but `LINE_JSON_REL` is in the PR at plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/working_refs.py:27. tests/mods/test_working_refs_contract.py pins `LINE_JSON_REL == mirror.LINE_JSON_PATH`, and nothing pins either of them to the widget's path. A rename that moves both producer sides in step passes every test while the ccstatusline widget keeps reading a file the mod no longer writes. The widget then falls back to the stale line.txt, or prints nothing.

Attack: Change `LINE_JSON_REL` in plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/working_refs.py:27 and `LINE_JSON_PATH` in plugins/working-refs/hooks/mirror.ts:22 to 'working-refs/line2.json', keeping the widget commandPath in plugins/banner-status/skills/setup-statusline/ccstatusline.defaults.json unchanged. Run `python -m pytest tests/skills/test_setup_statusline_contract.py tests/mods/test_working_refs_contract.py -q` and `claude plugin test plugins/working-refs`: every test passes. In a real session, though, the mod writes line2.json, the widget finds no line.json, and it prints the stale line.txt fallback and never the branch-stamped line.
fix: In tests/skills/test_setup_statusline_contract.py, import `LINE_JSON_REL` from `harness_lib.working_refs` and assert `_LINE_JSON == LINE_JSON_REL` (or use the import in place of the literal), then remove the outdated 'whether or not the harness constant has landed' comment.
Add `assert ts_string(mirror, "LINE_JSON_PATH") in <widget commandPath>` to tests/mods/test_working_refs_contract.py so the mirror, the harness constant and the widget form one chain.

minor.name: Test pins the repository's own .claude/ccstatusline.json to the plugin defaults
minor.summary: test_project_config_widget_matches_the_defaults (lines 242-245) reads _REPO/.claude/ccstatusline.json and requires its custom-command list to equal exactly the plugin defaults' widget. That file is this checkout's own dogfood configuration, not plugin content. CLAUDE.md says no test reads a real project checkout. If the developer adds a second custom-command widget or tunes the local statusline, a plugin contract test fails with no plugin defect behind it.
fix: Remove the test and keep .claude/ccstatusline.json in sync by hand or through the setup-statusline skill.
Relax it to check only that the defaults' commandPath appears among the project config's custom-command widgets, with a comment that it guards the repo's dogfood config.
